Multipurpose drain, e.g., 10.2 Fr; other common options include 8.5, 12, and 14 Fr. Select for the collection and contents.

obtain a scout CT. If using a physical grid, place it before scanning; otherwise use the virtual grid. Select a safe trajectory avoiding bowel, vessels, and other structures. Mark the skin entry site.
prep and drape the field. Create a lidocaine skin wheal and anesthetize along the planned tract.
a local-anesthetic needle may serve as a temporary marker. Obtain a CT check and adjust the entry angle as needed.

remove the marker needle and advance the access needle/coaxial introducer under intermittent CT or CT-fluoroscopy guidance. Confirm the tip within the collection, remove the stylet, and aspirate for confirmation and ordered studies.

gently advance the compatible short Amplatz wire into the collection. Stop if resistance occurs; reassess with imaging rather than forcing the wire. Confirm wire position before exchanging the needle.

flush the catheter and straighten it with the compatible stiffening cannula per the device instructions. Prepare the matched dilator. Measure skin-to-target depth to guide dilation and catheter advancement.
maintain wire access, remove the introducer, and make a skin nick as needed. Advance the dilator over the wire only to the planned depth, then remove it while holding the wire.

load the drain and stiffener over the wire. Advance under imaging to the planned depth. If using a tee-off technique, hold the stiffener stationary while advancing the catheter off it; do not advance the rigid tip beyond the collection.

remove the wire and stiffener, allowing the pigtail to form within the collection. Gently tension and lock the retention suture per the device instructions; confirm the loop and sideholes are within the collection.
suture the drain, connect the drainage bag, and apply a dressing. Obtain a final CT to document position and assess for complications.

blocks.title: Routine orders
items: Diet - Outpatient: order regular diet. Inpatient: notify primary team diet is okay.
Vital signs per unit routine.
Tylenol 650 mg PRN.

blocks.title: Access care
items: Flush with 10 mL sterile saline twice daily.

blocks.title: Anticoagulation to resume
items: Warfarin: 24 hours.
IV unfractionated heparin: 6-8 hours.
Enoxaparin: 12 hours.
DOACs: Typically 24 hours; confirm agent and renal function.
Clopidogrel: 75 mg dose - 6 hours; 300-600 mg loading dose - 24 hours.
Aspirin: 24 hours.
Restart after hemostasis is confirmed; individualize timing for procedure-specific or patient-specific exceptions.

items: Discharge order with medication reconciliation - 30 minutes.
